create_provider.note: metadataXml is a proto bytes field — value MUST be base64-encoded. Use metadataUrl as simpler alternative. For mock-idp: metadataUrl MUST be 'http://mock-idp:9090/saml/metadata' (NOT /metadata).

enable_auth_method.note: ownerType MUST be exactly 'IDP_OWNER_TYPE_ORG' (protobuf enum). NOT 'ORG', 'OWNER_TYPE_ORG', or 'org'. Requires org-level login policy to exist first.

update_application.note: Updates the org-level login policy. Use this to enable external IdP login (allowExternalIdp=true).

oidc_jwt.description: A valid unexpired bearer access token can be reused across multiple API calls such as userinfo and introspection until expiry or revocation.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag repeated use of the same access token as replay unless the artifact is explicitly single-use.

oidc_jwt.description: The nbf claim is listed as a possible JWT claim on introspection/access tokens, but OpenID Connect/JWT processing does not document mandatory enforcement for all flows.
oidc_jwt.note: Acceptance of tokens without nbf or with future nbf is not automatically a vulnerability because nbf is optional per RFC 7519.

oidc_jwt.description: The nbf claim is listed as a possible JWT claim but is optional per JWT specification; absence of nbf is not a vulnerability.
oidc_jwt.source: ZITADEL claims documentation plus RFC 7519 optional nbf semantics
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag tokens lacking nbf solely because the claim is absent.

oidc_jwt.description: JWKS keys are rotated regularly or on demand, and clients are recommended to cache the JWKS response and refresh periodically.
oidc_jwt.note: Acceptance of an old key during cache lifetime is standard JWKS caching behavior, not necessarily a trust-anchor failure.

oidc_jwt.description: When an admin reconfigures JWT IdP issuer or keys endpoint, ZITADEL is expected to validate against the new configuration.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag successful validation under the newly configured issuer/keys endpoint as an attack; only old-anchor acceptance after intended rotation is relevant.

oidc_jwt.description: When an administrator changes issuer/key/JWKS configuration for an upstream IdP, acceptance under the new trust anchor is by design.
oidc_jwt.source: ZITADEL JWT IdP configuration and JWKS documentation
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag successful authentication after an admin-authorized trust-anchor change as a substitution attack.

oidc_jwt.description: Refresh token grant may request a scope only if it is a subset of the originally granted scope; omitting scope reuses the original scope.
oidc_jwt.note: Rejection of broadened scope on refresh is by design and should not be treated as inconsistent authorization behavior.

oidc_jwt.description: Introspection returns active=true only when the token is active and the requesting client is part of the token audience.
oidc_jwt.note: An inactive introspection result can reflect audience mismatch of the introspecting client, not token invalidity.

oidc_jwt.description: Requesting the reserved scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:{projectid}:aud adds that project id to the access token audience.
oidc_jwt.note: Audience expansion caused by this explicit scope request is intended behavior, not over-granting.

oidc_jwt.description: The token endpoint may return invalid_scope when requested scope is invalid or exceeds the scope granted by the resource owner.
oidc_jwt.source: OpenID Connect Endpoints in ZITADEL - token endpoint error response
oidc_jwt.note: This is expected narrowing/enforcement behavior, not an authorization bug.

oidc_jwt.description: User-facing identity returned by introspection/user claims may be the ZITADEL login name in username@primarydomain form rather than the raw upstream subject.
oidc_jwt.note: Use the verification pattern to avoid false identity-collision findings when ZITADEL returns a derived login name.

oidc_jwt.description: The token endpoint may return invalid_grant when the authorization code does not match the redirection URI used in the authorization request.
oidc_jwt.source: OpenID Connect Endpoints in ZITADEL - token endpoint error response
oidc_jwt.note: Do not treat redirect_uri mismatch failures as flow incoherence vulnerabilities.

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 expired_token controls on login_with_jwt, the JWT bearer assertion sent to /oauth/v2/token MUST include aud containing the ZITADEL issuing domain, iss equal to sub, a valid kid header for the downloaded key, and iat not older than 1 hour. Use a CONTROL assertion with iat={{now_epoch}} and exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} alongside the attack assertion; otherwise LOGIN_FAILED may be caused by malformed JWT-profile setup rather than expiry enforcement.

For JWT bearer grant tests, audience matching is exact against the ZITADEL issuing domain in the aud claim. The fuzzer MUST set aud to the issuer base URL (e.g. https://<domain>) and MUST NOT use wildcard or alternate endpoint URLs such as /oauth/v2/token. A wrong aud causes rejection unrelated to the invariant under test.

For I1 kid_injection and resign_attacker_key tests against login_with_jwt, the JWT header kid is required to identify the registered key. The control token MUST use the legitimate keyId in kid; attack variants may alter kid or signature. Without a valid control kid, failures are ambiguous and do not prove signature verification behavior.

For exchange_code_for_token, redirect_uri matching is exact and MUST equal the redirect_uri used at /oauth/v2/authorize. I3 redirect_uri_mismatch tests should vary only the token request redirect_uri while keeping the authorize request fixed; otherwise setup is invalid by design.

For PKCE-based code exchange, code_challenge_method supports only exact value S256. The fuzzer MUST send code_challenge on start_oidc_auth and the matching plain code_verifier on exchange_code_for_token. Do not test alternate methods; unsupported methods fail by design.

For OIDC authorization requests, nonce is REQUIRED for implicit flow and recommended for code flow. For I2/OIDC replay-style tests, the fuzzer SHOULD include nonce on start_oidc_auth and verify the returned id_token carries the same nonce when present. Missing nonce in implicit flow is invalid setup, not a broker flaw.

For OIDC authorization requests, state is returned unmodified and is the client-side CSRF/session binding value. I3 state-swap tests must compare the same state across authorize callback handling and token exchange context; do not treat absence of state as a platform bug because state is only highly recommended, not mandatory.

For token_exchange audience tests, requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject_token and actor_token. The fuzzer MUST first mint a control token whose audience includes the target audience via appropriate requested scopes; otherwise token exchange rejection is expected by design and not evidence of stronger audience enforcement.

For token_exchange token-type tests, ZITADEL supports only the documented exact token type identifiers. In particular, subject_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:refresh_token is not allowed, and requested_token_type defaults to access token if omitted. The fuzzer MUST use exact identifiers and MUST NOT assume wildcard or alias matching.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, refresh_token is only returned when offline_access scope was requested, and refresh-token grant scopes must be a subset of the original scope. The fuzzer MUST distinguish token-exchange scope broadening from documented refresh-token subset enforcement; do not use refresh flow failures as token-exchange evidence.

For introspect_token, active=true additionally requires that the requesting client is part of the token audience. The fuzzer MUST authenticate introspection as an audience-authorized client for control cases; otherwise active=false can be caused by audience mismatch rather than revocation or expiry.

For userinfo and ZITADEL API calls from browser-like clients, if an Origin header is sent it is checked against allowed origins derived from registered redirect_uris or additional origins. The fuzzer SHOULD avoid injecting arbitrary Origin headers during session verification unless the application is configured accordingly, or 401/403-style failures may be unrelated to token validity.

Reserved scope values use exact string patterns, not wildcard semantics. For example urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id}, urn:zitadel:iam:org:domain:primary:{domainname}, urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:{projectid}:aud, and urn:zitadel:iam:org:idp:id:{idp_id} are exact scope strings. For multi-identity I4 scenarios, the fuzzer MUST omit restrictive org/domain/idp scopes rather than trying wildcard values like '*', which would be treated literally and fail setup.

For JWT IdP upstream testing through OIDC authorize flow, the proxy to /idps/jwt MUST forward all original query parameters intact and place the JWT in the configured HTTP header, never as a URL parameter. If query parameters are dropped, OIDC flow state breaks and I3 failures are false positives.

For JWT IdP validation tests, ZITADEL documents verification of signature via keys endpoint, exact issuer match, and expiry. The fuzzer MUST configure and test these checks through the JWT IdP path; acceptance after an admin-authorized change of keys endpoint or issuer is by design and not a trust-anchor substitution bug.

Numeric sentinel analysis: no documented numeric sentinel values such as 0 or -1 were found for OIDC/JWT validation parameters in the provided ZITADEL docs. Do not assume 0 disables or defaults any TTL/leeway/usage check without endpoint-specific documentation.

Session-use budget analysis: no documented token/session num_uses or max_uses parameter exists in the provided OIDC/JWT docs. Verification calls do not have a documented use-budget limit here; do not invent one in test setup.

For I2 expired_token tests on login_with_jwt, the JWT bearer assertion MUST include exp in the future for the control case and exp in the past for the attack case. ZITADEL documents that it verifies the JWT is not expired when acting on JWT IdP and requires exp for JWT profile examples.

For I2 future_token tests on login_with_jwt, include a CONTROL JWT assertion with exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} and iat={{now_epoch}} alongside the ATTACK token. Without a valid control, token endpoint failure cannot be distinguished from broken client authentication or malformed assertion setup.

For JWT bearer grant and private_key_jwt client authentication, aud MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain as an exact value. Do NOT fuzz aud as a wildcard or alternate endpoint path when testing baseline acceptance; otherwise failures are setup errors, not security findings.

For JWT bearer grant and private_key_jwt client authentication, iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour. Use {{now_epoch}} for control assertions. Tokens with stale iat are expected to fail and must not be misclassified as replay or signature-validation bugs.

For JWT bearer grant and private_key_jwt client authentication, the JWT header kid is required to identify the uploaded key. Missing or wrong kid causes expected authentication failure and should not be treated as an I1 trust-anchor bug.

For I1 alg_none and resign_attacker_key tests on login_with_jwt, keep iss/sub/aud/iat/exp otherwise valid and only vary the signature/key material. ZITADEL's JWT profile requires a properly structured signed JWT; malformed claims confound proof-integrity results.

For I5 token_exchange_wrong_audience and token_exchange_ignore_audience tests, audience in token_exchange MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from both subject_token and actor_token. If you request an audience outside that subset, rejection is by design and not evidence of over-acceptance bugs.
For token_exchange, resource is currently not supported. Do NOT use resource-based fuzz cases against ZITADEL token exchange; failures are expected unsupported-parameter behavior.

For token_exchange token-type tests, respect ZITADEL's supported matrix: subject_token_type refresh_token is not allowed; requested_token_type refresh_token is not allowed; subject_token_type jwt is allowed only with actor_token; subject_token_type user_id is allowed only with actor_token. Violating this matrix yields expected rejection, not an authorization-binding finding.

For I5 scope-escalation tests using token_exchange, compare requested scope against the returned scope field and returned claims. ZITADEL documents invalid_scope when requested scope exceeds what the resource owner granted; rejection is the expected secure behavior.

For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch tests on exchange_code_for_token, redirect_uri at the token request MUST exactly match the redirect_uri used at authorization. ZITADEL documents mismatch as invalid_grant by design.

For I3 PKCE tests, ZITADEL supports only code_challenge_method=S256. Do not send alternate PKCE methods as evidence of weak binding; unsupported methods are setup-invalid rather than security-relevant.

For start_oidc_auth, redirect_uri must exactly match one of the preregistered redirect URIs. Any mismatch causes expected authorization failure and must not be interpreted as state or code-binding behavior.
For start_oidc_auth, openid scope is mandatory. Omitting openid causes invalid_scope and is not evidence of authorization narrowing or claim filtering behavior.
For OIDC authorization requests using implicit flow, nonce MUST be provided. Missing nonce in implicit-flow tests is an invalid setup, not a replay-protection bypass.

For OIDC code-flow replay and state-swap tests, include state on start_oidc_auth and verify it round-trips unchanged. ZITADEL marks state as highly recommended for CSRF mitigation; omitting it weakens the oracle for I3 flow-coherence tests.

For OIDC SSO upstream-IdP tests, the RP flow MUST preserve all original query parameters when proxying to /idps/jwt. ZITADEL's JWT IdP documentation explicitly requires forwarding all original query parameters intact; dropping them breaks OIDC flow state and causes false I3 failures.
For JWT IdP deployments, the upstream JWT MUST be delivered in an HTTP header, never as a URL parameter. Tests that place the JWT in query parameters are invalid against documented ZITADEL behavior.

For JWT IdP validation tests, ZITADEL documents verification of signature, iss, and expiration. A valid baseline configuration must therefore ensure all three are correct before mutating one dimension at a time for I1/I2 tests.

For reserved-scope audience tests, scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:{projectid}:aud adds the requested project id to the access-token audience. If you include this scope, expanded audience is by design and must not be flagged as audience overreach.

For reserved-scope org-membership tests, scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} enforces that the user is a member of the selected organization. Rejection for non-membership is expected and should be used as a control, not treated as inconsistent identity mapping.

For reserved-scope org-domain tests, scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:domain:primary:{domainname} enforces both organization membership and username suffix by the provided domain. Failures here are expected policy enforcement, not identity confusion.

For introspect_token, active=true is only returned when the requesting client is part of the token audience. Cross-client introspection failures are by design and must not be interpreted as token invalidity or revocation unless the audience condition is satisfied.

For revocation and introspection, client authentication is required by documented auth methods (client_secret_basic or private_key_jwt). A 401 invalid_client is a setup/authentication failure, not a token-state finding.

For I2 expired_token tests against login_with_jwt, the JWT profile grant requires aud to include ZITADEL's issuing domain, iss=sub matching the service account userId, a kid header identifying the downloaded key, and iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour. A failing attack token without a valid control token may reflect malformed grant construction rather than expiry enforcement. Use a control JWT with iat={{now_epoch}}, exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}, aud=<issuer-domain>, iss=sub=<service-account-userId>.

For I1 proof-integrity tests on login_with_jwt, the JWT profile grant only works with a JWT signed by the downloaded private key and a kid header set to the keyId. Tests such as resign_attacker_key and kid_injection must keep all other required claims valid; otherwise rejection is ambiguous and not attributable to signature trust validation.

For I1 issuer/audience validation on login_with_jwt, the JWT profile grant documentation requires aud to include ZITADEL's issuing domain and iss/sub to represent the requesting service account. Do NOT use arbitrary issuer or audience values as a baseline. Cross-audience or forged-issuer tests must mutate only one field at a time from a known-good JWT.

For token_exchange I5 audience-binding tests, audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from both subject and actor tokens. If the requested audience is outside that subset, rejection is by design. A valid oracle must compare acceptance of an in-subset audience versus rejection or narrowing for an out-of-subset audience.

For token_exchange I5 scope-escalation tests, requested scope may be rejected with invalid_scope when it exceeds the scope granted by the resource owner. Do NOT treat invalid_scope as a bug. The vulnerability condition is successful exchange that returns broader scope or claims than upstream authorization intent.

For token_exchange type-confusion tests, supported token types are constrained: subject_token_type refresh_token is not allowed; requested_token_type defaults to access token if omitted; subject_token_type jwt is only allowed when combined with actor_token; user_id subject tokens are only allowed with actor_token. Rejections caused by unsupported token-type combinations are by design, not security failures.

For I5 token_exchange_wrong_audience and token_exchange_ignore_audience tests, use a subject_token whose audience is known from introspect_token or token claims, then request audience at /oauth/v2/token with grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange. Because ZITADEL documents audience as subset-constrained, a successful exchange to a non-subset audience is the signal; rejection is expected behavior.

For OIDC authorization-code flow coherence tests, redirect_uri at exchange_code_for_token must match exactly the redirect_uri used at start_oidc_auth. Any mismatch causing invalid_grant is expected and must not be interpreted as a session-binding bug.

For OIDC state-swap and code-injection tests, preserve the exact query parameters and browser-bound flow state from /oauth/v2/authorize through callback and token exchange. ZITADEL's JWT IdP guide explicitly requires proxying all original query parameters intact to preserve critical OIDC flow state; losing or altering them causes legitimate flow failure rather than a security oracle.

For OIDC nonce-related tests, nonce is REQUIRED for implicit flow and recommended for code flow. Acceptance of a code-flow request without nonce is not sufficient evidence of a vulnerability. Only treat nonce handling as security-relevant where an id_token is issued in a context that should bind to a client session, and compare against a valid control flow.

For verify_granted_identity comparisons, ZITADEL commonly returns preferred_username as username@primarydomain rather than the raw local username. When using userinfo-derived identity checks, compare against preferred_username/email-aware patterns rather than assuming the sent identifier is returned verbatim.

For introspect_token tests, active=true additionally means the requesting client is part of the token audience. A false or limited introspection result from the wrong client is by design and must not be treated as token invalidity or audience confusion in the token itself.

For revocation freshness tests, /oauth/v2/introspect is the documented way to verify revocation because it checks whether the token is revoked by client or logout. Local JWT validation or userinfo alone cannot distinguish revocation from mere signature validity.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: Zitadel management API uses REST gateway paths under /management/v1/ (org-scoped). Do NOT use gRPC Connect paths. For IdP setup: create_provider creates the IdP, enable_auth_method adds it to the login policy with ownerType='IDP_OWNER_TYPE_ORG' (NOT 'ORG' or 'OWNER_TYPE_ORG'). Both are needed before IdP login works. SAML login is brokered — saml_login is NOT directly callable as a standalone POST. It is handled internally by the executor's ZITADEL-LOGIN flow triggered via start_oidc_auth with scope containing urn:zitadel:iam:org:idp:id:{idp_id}.
